countingMethod: Reviewed claim groups: ten narrative/code mechanism groups per lesson; one answer-key, each option explanation, and one worked-reasoning group per question; one sourced definition/alias group per glossary term; one analogy inclusion/mapping/limit decision per active lesson. Counts describe review groups, not distinct scientific facts.
corrections: Clarified omitted effect dependencies from “Run after every commit” to commits of this component, avoiding an application-wide timing interpretation.
Qualified “Setters belong in handlers” as “Handlers may call setters”; setters can also be valid in effect logic, so the original takeaway implied an unnecessarily exclusive location.
Changed the ref-versus-state quiz from a completed-task total to an independent changing score, avoiding an implication that a count derived from existing task state should be stored redundantly.
Narrowed Top-level Hook call aliases to precise Hook phrases so ordinary top-level component definitions do not open an unrelated Hook-call definition.
Rephrased project setup and module-level imported helper to avoid effect-setup and global-variable dictionary targets with the wrong sense.

Added three missing JavaScript glossary entries for try...catch, Error constructor and object property shorthand; expanded the fetch explanation to distinguish creating, throwing and catching an error.
gaps: Mounted React checks run against React/React DOM19.3.1 in jsdom; real study-app mobile/desktop and offline integration remains root verification work.
The client-only fetch assumes a same-origin array/id/text contract and does not implement production caching, request sharing, schema validation, authentication or cancellation.
AbortController cancellation is defined and distinguished from ignoring a result, but is not implemented in the teaching component.
Performance explanations and Compiler configuration are sourced as of this review, without claiming a measured speedup or executing React Compiler in this scratch harness.
The final task project implements search and completion toggles. Add-task UI and persistence are explicitly labelled extensions rather than implemented features.

analogyReview.scope: Fresh independent check of all six existing analogy mappings and limits, all nine decisions and question prerequisites with disclosures closed.

rh-hook-rules.rationale: Numbered seats map successive ordinary Hook calls to stable positions; the limit correctly excludes variable names and literal theatre allocation. All call rules remain visible.

rh-refs-dom.rationale: A bookmark captures persistence without requesting rewritten output; the limit states that refs can hold arbitrary values and React manages DOM refs during commit.

rh-effects-cleanup.rationale: Library borrowing and returning models acquiring and releasing the exact prior resource before replacement and final removal; the limit explicitly avoids claiming all effects need cleanup.

rh-effect-dependencies.rationale: The concrete music-to-books connection trace and three dependency choices teach dependency identity directly; another resource comparison would repeat the preceding cleanup analogy.

rh-fetch-lifecycle.rationale: An obsolete takeaway reply models ignoring stale response application; the visible limit correctly rejects cancellation of network/server work. Request ordering, errors and empty/loading facts stay outside the disclosure.

rh-custom-hooks.rationale: Two kitchens following one recipe distinguish reused logic from independent local state; the explicit shared-external-source limit is accurate for two browser event subscriptions.

rh-context.rationale: Local noticeboards map the nearest-provider override, while the limit locates ancestry in the React tree rather than physical or CSS distance.

rh-performance.rationale: The three-tool table and exact immutable dependency example supply a precise distinction; a generic caching comparison would add no mechanism or measured evidence.

rh-practice-project.rationale: This integration lesson applies concepts already given analogies and supplies a concrete behavioural checklist. Repeating comparisons would lengthen the complete example without explaining a new concept.

conceptFirstReview.scope: Independent concept-first review of all nine active lessons, all 27 question keys and 108 options, 52 local glossary entries, retained code and analogy prerequisites. Original factual review and unchanged glossary provenance remain intact; this record documents the current editorial classifications and targeted corrections.
conceptFirstReview.countingMethod: 94 review units: nine lesson mechanism/classification bundles, 27 question contracts including all options and walkthroughs, 52 glossary entries, six analogy mappings/limits. Three corrections comprise two dictionary target corrections and one standalone-question clarification; the arithmetic-to-prediction rewrite is editorial, not counted as an accuracy correction.

corrections.detail: Added try block/try blocks aliases so JavaScript error-handling prose opens the JavaScript entry instead of a Python fallback; independently checked MDN try...catch.
Made the useState-backed implementation explicit in the prompt, removing reliance on recalling the lesson and avoiding a universal claim about custom Hooks that use shared external stores.

Added asynchronous work alias to the local Promise/await entry. The previous cross-subject fallback described queued fire-and-forget work shielding the caller from worker failures, which does not describe this fetch example.

rh-hook-rules.rationale: No mathematical formulas needed: stable call order and tree position are behavioural concepts. Retain the short Counter JSX to trace null output versus removal. All three unchanged questions test state preservation, legal call locations and repairing conditional Hooks; visible prose supplies the prerequisites.

rh-refs-dom.rationale: No formulas needed. Retain the focused DOM example because ref attachment and focus are the objective. All three unchanged questions distinguish display state from persistent ref storage, predict focus and diagnose unsafe DOM manipulation; no optional panel is required.

rh-effects-cleanup.rationale: No equations needed for resource lifecycle. Retain the exact listener setup/cleanup example to identify callback ownership. Three unchanged questions choose effect-worthy work, order old cleanup before new setup and interpret development Strict Mode without claiming production render counts.

rh-effect-dependencies.rationale: No equations needed. The small room component and concrete reconnect trace teach identity comparison and stale closure directly. Three unchanged questions diagnose missing inputs, simplify a fresh-object dependency and remove redundant derived state; the trace is complete without an analogy.

rh-fetch-lifecycle.rationale: No formulas needed. Retain the complete fetch component because per-setup flags, HTTP errors and guarded success/error branches are the mechanism under study. Three unchanged questions predict response ordering, distinguish HTTP failure from Promise rejection and select observable lifecycle checks; contract and cancellation limits remain visible.

rh-custom-hooks.rationale: No mathematical formulas needed; the increments are executable code illustrating local state, not a maths exercise. Retain both short Hook examples to show independent state and subscriptions. Rewrite q1 from arithmetic output to a prediction about which caller changes, explicitly stating local useState in the prompt. Unchanged q2/q3 test subscription ownership and useful Hook interfaces/cleanup.

questionsRewritten.rh-custom-hooks-q1: Replace repeated step arithmetic with independent-local-state prediction. Explicitly describe useState and the increment handler so the standalone question does not assume all custom Hooks avoid shared external sources; preserve its id, owner, option count and correct index.

rh-context.rationale: No equations needed. Retain the small nested-provider example so nearest ancestry and fallback can be traced. All three unchanged questions predict provider values, explain memoised consumer updates and choose sensible context ownership; default/provider facts remain in visible prose.

rh-performance.rationale: No formulas or invented timings. Retain useMemo and useCallback snippets because dependency identity and functional updates are the mechanisms being contrasted. Three unchanged questions choose measurement, distinguish the caches and diagnose in-place mutation. No measured speedup or compiler execution is asserted.

rh-practice-project.rationale: No formulas needed. Retain the complete small app because composing state, filtering and immutable toggles is the objective. The three unchanged questions predict filtered-toggle results, choose minimal state and diagnose loss of removed row-local state; the behavioural checklist supplies direct evidence without extra analogies.
